newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 watch markets after Greenspan shock - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: G10 watch markets after Greenspan shock - Tietmeyer.

text.p: The Group of 10 central bank will continue to watch financial market developments carefully, but central bankers feel that last week's reaction to Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks was somewhat excessive.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, who is chairman of the G10 central bank governors committee, added that markets seemed to be stable.

Tietmeyer also told reporters at the Bank for International Settlements that there had indeed been some improvement in economic fundamentals during the last year and this was also reflected in financial markets.
The reaction of financial markets on Friday to Greenspan's remarks about "irrational exuberance" in asset markets was among the topics discussed by G10 central bankers today.
Tietmeyer noted the central bankers had discussed not only last week's events in financial markets, but also longer-term developments.

"We feel to some extent there was an over-reaction to a question and the markets seem to be stable again," Tietmeyer said. In his "over-reaction" comment, Tietmeyer characterised the Greenspan remarks last week as a question.

"Looking at the developments of the last year, we should not overlook that there is some improvement in the fundamentals and this is to some extent reflected in the developments of the financial market, but we will of course watch further developments very carefully," Tietmeyer said.
